stays.name: Hotel Palm Royal Resort Kokusai Street

location.name: Hotel Palm Royal Resort Kokusai Street
location.address: 3-9-10 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa 900-0013

stays.notes:
2 adults, 3 nights, no meals. Check-in 3:00 PM – midnight; checkout by 11 AM (leave early Nov 2 for the ferry). ¥68,720. Free cancellation through Oct 26.

Japanese name for taxis: ホテルパームロイヤルリゾート国際通り. +81 98-865-5551. 4-min walk from Makishi monorail station. Ask to store bags before check-in on Oct 30 (a request, not confirmed).

Well positioned for the Nov 1 procession on Kokusai-dori.

stays.name: Tokashiku Marine Village
stays.roomType: Japanese-Style Triple Room with Sea View (3 futons)
stays.notes:
2 adults, 3 futons. Check-in 3:00 – 6:00 PM; checkout by 11 AM. Breakfast and dinner included (breakfast 7–9 AM, dinner 6–8:30 PM). ¥36,766. Free cancellation through Oct 29.

Shuttle to/from Tokashiki Port (~10 min). **Before travel, call +81 98-987-2426** with the Nov 2 9:40 AM arrival and Nov 3 5:00 PM ferry; confirm return shuttle time, luggage storage and post-checkout showers. Ask about snorkel operators.

stays.name: Ryukyu Hotel & Resort Nashiro Beach
stays.notes: 2 adults. Breakfast included. Wedding stay — **wedding day is Nov 4**. Arriving in the evening Nov 3 by taxi from Tomari Port; tell the hotel.

stays.name: Anse Yomitan Toya

location.name: Anse Yomitan Toya
location.address: 20 Toya, Yomitan, Nakagami District, Okinawa 904-0305, Japan

stays.roomType: Ocean King Room with Jacuzzi Bath
stays.notes: Sea view. Check-in 3:00 – 11:30 PM; checkout Nov 6 by 11 AM. No meals. Free parking.

stays.name: The Lodge Okinawa

location.name: The Lodge Okinawa
location.address: 1563 Imadomari, Nakijin, Okinawa

stays.roomType: Tent / glamping-style unit, queen bed, sauna
stays.notes:
2 nights. Check-in 3:00 – 7:00 PM; checkout Nov 8 by 10 AM. No meals. Free parking. Shared bathroom/toilet. ¥55,440 total. Free cancellation through Oct 22, 11:59 PM JST (¥27,720 from Oct 23).

**¥15,000 refundable damage deposit by card at arrival** — ask how it's refunded. +81 980-43-1300. Tell them ~4:30 PM arrival.

stays.name: Hotel Nikko Taipei

location.name: Hotel Royal-Nikko Taipei
location.address: No. 37-1, Section 2, Chung Shan North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei City 104, Taiwan

stays.notes:
Booked via Booking.com (listed as Hotel Royal-Nikko Taipei). 2 adults, no breakfast. Booking PIN 9273. TWD 22,585 total, prepaid in full at any time.

Free cancellation through Nov 5, 2026, 11:59 PM Taipei time; after that, no changes and the full amount is forfeited.

Pool is closed for seasonal maintenance during the stay. Bring toiletries, photo ID and the card used to book for check-in. About a 3-minute walk from Zhongshan MRT Exit 3.

stays.name: JR Kyushu Hotel Blossom Naha

location.name: JR Kyushu Hotel Blossom Naha
location.address: 2-16-1 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa

stays.notes:
Check-in 3:00 – 11:00 PM; checkout Nov 13 5:00 – 11:00 AM. Breakfast included.

Arriving ~10–10:30 PM off IT232 — tell the hotel and confirm late-arrival procedure. JR九州ホテル ブラッサム那覇. 5-min walk from Miebashi monorail station.

travels.title: Chicago → Taipei
travels.notes:
Our big send-off. The flight leaves at 12:30 AM, so we head to O'Hare the evening of **Oct 28** and aim to be there around 9:30 PM. EVA Air flies from Terminal 5 (international). At the counter, ask them to check our bags all the way to Naha and print the BR112 boarding pass too, so Taipei is just a quick walk between gates.

Ticket 695 2464270937 · 2 checked bags.

travels.title: Taipei → Naha
travels.notes:
A short hop to Okinawa. At Taoyuan we stay airside: follow the **Transfer** signs, go through the transfer security check, then find BR112's gate on the departure boards. Bags should be checked through, so no need to collect them.

Ticket 695 2464270937 · 2 checked bags.

travels.title: Tomari Port → Tokashiki Port
travels.notes:
A 40-minute high-speed boat across turquoise water to the Kerama Islands.

**Getting on:** the Marine Liner Tokashiki leaves from the north side of Tomari Port which isn't the same berth as the big car ferry — tell the taxi "Tokashiki Marine Liner." Go to the ferry counter, show reservation **TK11020064**, and pay for/collect the tickets there (recorded ¥12,740 return for two; fares changed Oct 1, so it may differ a little). Boarding starts 30 minutes before departure and everyone must be aboard 10 minutes before. Sailing status is posted around 8 AM.

travels.title: Tokashiki Port → Tomari Port
travels.notes: Back to Naha, salty and sun-tired. The hotel shuttle drops us at the port around 3:30–4 PM; pick up return tickets at the counter and be aboard by 4:50. In Naha, walk out of the terminal to the taxi rank (or meet a pre-arranged taxi) for the ride south to the wedding hotel.

travels.title: Tomari Port → Ryukyu Hotel
travels.notes: About an hour south down the coast to Itoman. Ask the resort to arrange it ahead, or grab a taxi from the Tomari Port rank and show them the hotel name. Let the hotel know we're arriving in the evening.

travels.title: Naha → Taipei
travels.notes: Goodbye Okinawa, hello Taiwan — it's only a 1.5-hour flight, and we gain an hour (Taiwan is one hour behind Japan). Be at Naha's international departures by 6:45–7:00 AM; check the Tigerair baggage allowance before we pack.

travels.title: Taipei → Naha
travels.notes: Back to Okinawa for one last night. Be at Taoyuan Terminal 1 by ~3:15 PM; we gain the hour back on arrival.

travels.title: Naha → Taipei
travels.notes:
The first leg home. Ask at check-in to send our bags straight through to Chicago.

Ticket 695 2464270937 · 2 checked bags.

travels.title: Taipei → Chicago
travels.notes:
The long flight home, landing the same evening thanks to the date line. In Taipei follow the Transfer signs to the gate.

Ticket 695 2464270937 · 2 checked bags.

days.title: Off we go
days.summary: The adventure starts with a late-night flight out of O'Hare. We sleep somewhere over the Pacific, change planes in Taipei, and wake up headed for the subtropical islands of Okinawa.

days.title: Hello, Naha
days.summary: We land in Okinawa's capital mid-morning, ride the little elevated monorail into town and drop our bags. Then it's an easy first day on foot: a lively shopping street, a buzzing fish market for lunch, a quiet old pottery quarter and our first Okinawan dinner. No pressure — if we're tired, we just do less.

items.title: Through the airport
items.notes: Immigration, bags and customs — allow about an hour. Then follow the signs for **Yui Rail / Monorail (ゆいレール)**: a signed walkway leads straight from the terminal to Naha Airport Station. No shuttle needed.

items.title: Monorail into town

location.name: Naha Airport Station
location.address: Kagamizu, Naha, Okinawa 901-0142, Japan

items.notes: At the ticket machines, buy two one-way tickets to **Makishi (牧志), station 09** — ¥320 each. The ticket has a QR code: scan it at the gate going in and keep it to get out. Board toward **Tedako-Uranishi**; it's the only direction from the airport. Ride 8 stops (~16 min, no transfers), with views over the city as we go. Makishi is right after Miebashi.

items.title: Walk to the hotel and drop our bags

location.name: Hotel Palm Royal Resort Kokusai Street
location.address: 3-9-10 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa 900-0013

items.notes: From Makishi Station take the elevator down, then a 4-minute walk along Kokusai-dori to Palm Royal. Ask reception to keep our luggage until check-in and head straight back out. Backup if we're wiped out: a 15-minute taxi from the airport, showing the hotel name ホテルパームロイヤルリゾート国際通り.

items.title: Kokusai-dori

location.name: Kokusai Street
location.address: Kokusai-dori, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

items.notes: "International Street" — Naha's colorful main drag, a mile of snack stands, souvenir shops and people-watching. Just a gentle first wander; we'll turn off into the market arcades before long.

items.title: Makishi Public Market + lunch

location.name: Makishi Public Market
location.address: 2-chōme-10-1 Matsuo, Naha, Okinawa 900-0014, Japan

items.notes: Naha's kitchen. Downstairs, stalls piled with tropical fish in impossible colors, lobster and island pork. The fun trick: buy seafood downstairs and have a restaurant upstairs cook it for us (ask the price first). Afterwards, get lost in the covered Heiwa-dori arcade and the indie cafés of Ukishima-dori.

items.title: Tsuboya pottery street + café break

location.name: Tsuboya Yachimun Street
location.address: 1 Chome-16 Tsuboya, Naha, Okinawa 902-0065, Japan

items.notes: One of the highlights of the day. A stone-paved lane where potters have worked for over 300 years, lined with shops of hand-thrown bowls and cups and the odd shisa lion on a rooftop. Find a café and try **buku-buku cha**, a Ryukyuan tea whipped into a tall cloud of foam.

items.title: Sakurazaka side streets

location.name: Sakurazaka Theater
location.address: 3-chōme-6-10 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa 900-0013, Japan

items.notes: A little arty pocket of tiny bars and shops around an indie theater, on our way back. The first thing to skip if we're fading.

items.title: Check in and freshen up

location.name: Hotel Palm Royal Resort Kokusai Street
location.address: 3-9-10 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa 900-0013

items.notes: Collect the bags, shower off the flight. Check-in is open until midnight, so we can stay out longer if the afternoon's going well.

items.title: Our first Okinawan dinner
items.notes: A casual izakaya near the hotel. Things to try: **Okinawa soba** (chewy noodles in pork broth), **rafute** (melt-in-your-mouth braised pork belly), **goya champuru** (bitter melon stir-fry — an Okinawan icon) and **jimami tofu** (silky peanut tofu).

days.title: Naha history: the Ryukyu Kingdom
days.summary: For 450 years Okinawa was its own kingdom, the Ryukyu Kingdom, trading with China, Japan and Southeast Asia. Today we visit its old royal capital at Shuri: a hilltop castle, a royal tomb, and an ancient cobbled lane winding down through the trees. In the afternoon, the island's story at the prefectural museum, then a lantern-lit market alley for dinner.

items.title: Monorail up to Shuri

location.name: Shuri Station
location.address: 3 Chome Shuriteracho, Naha, Okinawa 903-0806, Japan

items.notes: Breakfast near the hotel, then walk back to **Makishi Station** and ride toward Tedako-Uranishi to **Shuri (首里)**, 4 stops. From Shuri Station it's a ~20-minute walk uphill to the castle, following the signs.

items.title: Shuri Castle

location.name: Shuri Castle
location.address: 1-chōme-2 Shurikinjōchō, Naha, Okinawa 903-0815, Japan

items.notes: The red-lacquered palace of the Ryukyu kings, on a hill with views out to the sea. It burned in 2019 and is being rebuilt — the main hall reopens Nov 23, just after we leave — but the great stone walls, ceremonial gates and lookouts are open and we may see the restoration work. Paid area ¥400 each at the counter.

items.title: Tamaudun royal tomb

location.name: Tamaudun
location.address: Japan, 〒903-0815 沖縄県那覇市首里金城町１丁目３

items.notes: A short walk away: the stone mausoleum of the kings, built in 1501, guarded by carved lions. Quiet, shady, and a World Heritage site. ¥300 each.

items.title: The old stone road down the hill

location.name: Shuri Kinjo-cho Stone-Paved Road
location.address: 2 Chome Shurikinjocho, Naha, Okinawa 903-0815, Japan

items.notes: One of the prettiest walks in Okinawa: a 16th-century cobbled lane winding downhill between old stone walls, red-tiled roofs and huge banyan trees. Slippery if it rains. It ends at the bottom of the hill, away from the monorail — we'll grab a taxi from the main road to the museum.

items.title: Okinawa Prefectural Museum

location.name: Okinawa Prefectural Museum & Art Museum
location.address: 3-chōme-1-1 Omoromachi, Naha, Okinawa 900-0006, Japan

items.notes: The story of the islands, from coral reefs to kings to the war and after, in a striking fortress-like building. ¥530 each, **cash only**; ask for the English audio guide. Completely optional — swap for a nap if we need one.

items.title: Sakaemachi market + izakaya dinner

location.name: Sakaemachi Market
location.address: 381-379 Asato, Naha, Okinawa 902-0067, Japan

items.notes: An old covered market that comes alive at night, when its tiny stalls turn into bars and izakayas with just a few stools each. Wander, pick one that feels right, and settle in.

days.title: A royal parade on Kokusai-dori
days.summary: A Chinese garden in the morning, then the big event: the Ryukyu Dynasty Picture Scroll Procession, when about 700 people in royal court costume parade down Kokusai-dori — right outside our hotel. Then dinner out.

items.title: Fukushuen Garden

location.name: Fukushuen
location.address: 2-29-19 Kume, Naha

items.notes: A walled Chinese garden of koi ponds, pavilions and a little waterfall, a gift celebrating Naha's centuries-old ties with Fuzhou. About a 30-minute walk from the hotel (or a short taxi). ¥200 each.

items.title: Stroll around Kume
items.notes: The neighborhood where Chinese scholars and envoys once lived. If we're ahead of time, keep wandering into Wakasa.

items.title: Early lunch
items.notes: Eat, top up water and find a restroom before the crowds.

items.title: Ryukyu Dynasty Picture Scroll Procession

location.name: Kokusai Street
location.address: Kokusai-dori, Naha, Okinawa, Japan

items.notes: The highlight of the Shurijo Castle Festival: a king and queen, court officials, Chinese envoys, musicians and dancers in brilliant silk, bringing an old painted scroll to life. Free. Find a spot along the street by noon — roads close then, so we walk.

items.title: Prep for the island
items.notes: Pack a small beach bag for tomorrow and check the ferry and hotel shuttle are all set.

items.title: Dinner
items.notes: We already have a dinner plan for tonight — restaurant and time to be filled in.

days.title: Island time on Tokashiki
days.summary: A fast boat takes us out to Tokashiki, a small island in the Kerama chain — famous for some of the clearest water in the world, coral reefs and sea turtles. Our guesthouse sits right on the beach. Swim, snorkel, nap, eat a big dinner. That's the whole plan.

items.title: Taxi to Tomari Port
items.notes: Check out and have reception call us a taxi to the **Tokashiki Marine Liner** at Tomari Port (north side) — about 15–20 minutes. Keep swimsuits in a day bag, separate from luggage. At the port: show our booking at the counter, collect tickets, and board from 8:30.

items.title: Hotel shuttle to the beach
items.notes: Tokashiku Marine Village's shuttle meets the boat for a 10-minute ride across the island's green hills. Drop the bags at reception and go find the sand.

items.title: Tokashiku Beach

location.name: Tokashiku Beach
location.address: 1919-1 Tokashiki, Shimajiri District, Okinawa 901-3501, Japan

items.notes: A long, curving white-sand beach on a calm bay, right outside our door. Ask the marine desk about snorkel gear and what the water's like.

items.title: Lunch
items.notes: The hotel serves lunch from noon to 2.

items.title: Snorkel with turtles (hopefully)
items.notes: Sea turtles graze the seagrass in this bay. Options: a guided snorkel, a turtle-focused trip, or Aharen Beach on the other side of the island. The hotel books its own trips the day before. Or just float.

items.title: Check in, shower, rest
items.notes: A Japanese-style room with futons and a sea view.

items.title: Dinner at the guesthouse
items.notes: Dinner's included — island home cooking. Ask reception what time they're serving.

days.title: One last swim, then the wedding hotel
days.summary: We squeeze every drop out of Tokashiki — breakfast, beach, lunch, more beach — before the evening boat back to Naha and a taxi down to our resort in Itoman for the wedding.

items.title: Breakfast
items.notes: Included.

items.title: Morning swim or snorkel
items.notes: A second chance at the turtles if yesterday didn't work out.

items.title: Pack and check out
items.notes: The hotel holds our bags; keep a change of clothes and toiletries handy.

items.title: Shower and change
items.notes: Outdoor showers at the hotel, then collect the bags.

items.title: Shuttle back to the port
items.notes: The hotel tells us the exact time. Collect return tickets at the counter; aboard by 4:50.

items.title: Dinner
items.notes: Settle into the resort and see what the restaurants — or the wedding group — are up to.

days.title: The wedding
days.summary: The reason for the whole trip. A slow morning by the sea at the resort, then celebrating the happy couple. Times to come from the invitation.

items.title: Breakfast
items.notes: Included at the resort.

items.title: Wedding
items.notes: Ceremony and reception details to come. Check the dress code and whether transport's arranged.

days.title: Glass, pottery and a sunset cape
days.summary: We pick up a rental car and head north into Okinawa's craft country: glassblowers turning recycled bottles into bright blue glass, a village of potters and wood-fired kilns, and a wild clifftop cape for sunset. Tonight, a room with a jacuzzi looking out at the sea.

items.title: Pick up the rental car
items.notes: Check out of the resort and collect the car (booking to come: small automatic with an ETC toll card). Bring the International Driving Permit, license and passports. Driving is on the left.

items.title: Ryukyu Glass Village

location.name: Ryukyu Glass Village
location.address: 169 Fukuji, Itoman, Okinawa 901-0345, Japan

items.notes: Okinawa's biggest glass workshop: watch artisans blow molten glass, then browse bubbly blue, green and amber cups and lamps. The tradition started after the war, using old soda and beer bottles. Free entry.

items.title: Drive north
items.notes: About 1¾ hours up the west coast to Yomitan, through Naha and along Route 58. Optional detour: Mihama American Village in Chatan.

items.title: Yachimun no Sato pottery village

location.name: Yachimun no Sato
location.address: 2653-1番地 Zakimi, Yomitan, Nakagami District, Okinawa 904-0301, Japan

items.notes: A peaceful village of 19 pottery workshops and giant stepped wood-fired kilns, tucked among trees and red-tiled roofs. Wander between studios and maybe find a bowl to bring home.

items.title: Sunset at Cape Zanpa

location.name: Cape Zanpa
location.address: 675-1861 Uza, Yomitan, Nakagami District, Okinawa 904-0328, Japan

items.notes: Dramatic coral-limestone cliffs, crashing waves and a white lighthouse — the classic sunset spot on this coast. Arrive 30–45 minutes before sunset.

items.title: Optional: Mihama American Village

location.name: Mihama American Village
location.address: Mihama, Chatan, Nakagami District, Okinawa 904-0115, Japan

items.notes: A colorful seaside shopping-and-food district with a boardwalk, shaped by the nearby US bases. Fun, but it would need 2–3 hours, so it replaces something else.

items.title: Alternative: Zakimi Castle

location.name: Zakimi Castle Ruins
location.address: Japan, 〒904-0301 Okinawa, Nakagami District, Yomitan, Zakimi, ７０８ ６

items.notes: Beautifully curved 15th-century stone walls with hilltop views. Free.

days.title: Whale sharks and castle walls
days.summary: A morning at Churaumi, one of the world's great aquariums, where whale sharks and manta rays glide past one enormous window. Then a stroll down a tunnel of ancient trees in a fishing village, a castle ruin in the clouds, and our first night glamping in the north.

items.title: Drive to Churaumi
items.notes: Check out early and drive about 1½–2 hours up the coast road past Onna's beaches and through Nago.

items.title: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium

location.name: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium
location.address: 424 Ishikawa, Motobu, Kunigami District, Okinawa 905-0206, Japan

items.notes: The Kuroshio Sea tank is the showstopper — whale sharks and mantas swimming overhead. Also a living coral reef and sea turtles. ¥2,180 each.

items.title: Lunch
items.notes: In Ocean Expo Park, by the sea.

items.title: Bise Fukugi Tree Road

location.name: Bise Fukugi Tree Road
location.address: 389 Bise, Motobu, Kunigami District, Okinawa 905-0207, Japan

items.notes: Sandy lanes through a village shaded by 20,000 fukugi trees, planted 300 years ago as typhoon windbreaks, opening onto the sea. Optional if the aquarium runs long.

items.title: Nakijin Castle

location.name: Nakijin Castle Ruins
location.address: 5101 Imadomari, Nakijin, Kunigami District, Okinawa 905-0428, Japan

items.notes: Over a mile of snaking stone walls along a hilltop, older than Shuri, with views over the East China Sea. ¥1,000 each; wear good shoes.

items.title: Glamping at The Lodge

location.name: The Lodge Okinawa
location.address: 1563 Imadomari, Nakijin, Okinawa

items.notes: Our tent for two nights, with a queen bed and a sauna. Five minutes from the castle.

items.title: Dinner
items.notes: No meals at the Lodge — eat out nearby and pick up breakfast for tomorrow.

days.title: Seeing north Okinawa
days.summary: A road trip into Yanbaru, the wild, jungly north — a forest so rich it's a World Heritage site, home to birds found nowhere else. A sleepy village famous for long lives, a hike through giant limestone rocks, and the windswept northern tip of the island.

items.title: Drive to Ogimi
items.notes: About an hour up Route 58 along the coast.

items.title: Ogimi village

location.name: Shioya, Ogimi
location.address: Shioya, Ogimi Village, Kunigami District, Okinawa 905-1311, Japan

items.notes: A quiet seaside village known for its centenarians. Wander a bit, find coffee if anything's open.

items.title: ASMUI Spiritual Hikes

location.name: ASMUI Spiritual Trail
location.address: 1241 Ginama, Kunigami, Kunigami District, Okinawa 905-1422, Japan

items.notes: Paths through jungle and towering jagged limestone, with sacred sites and huge banyan trees. A shuttle takes us up; the main loop is about an hour. ¥2,500 each; download the audio guide before we lose signal.

items.title: Lunch
items.notes: Food up here is limited — bring snacks.

items.title: Cape Hedo

location.name: Cape Hedo
location.address: Hedo, Kunigami, Kunigami District, Okinawa 905-1421, Japan

items.notes: The northern tip of Okinawa: grassy cliffs over crashing surf and, on a clear day, the next island across the water.

items.title: Drive back to the Lodge
items.notes: Back down Route 58 with a stop or two. Sauna time.

days.title: Mangroves by kayak
days.summary: We paddle a guided kayak through a mangrove forest on Okinawa's east coast — a quiet, green world of tangled roots, crabs and wading birds, completely different from the reefs. Then a long drive south to Naha to return the car. (Tonight's hotel isn't booked yet.)

items.title: Drive to Gesashi
items.notes: Check out of the Lodge, then about an hour across the island to the east coast.

items.title: Mangrove kayaking

location.name: Yanbaru Nature School
location.address: 82 Gesashi, Higashi, Okinawa 905-1205

items.notes: A two-hour guided paddle up the Gesashi River at high tide. The tide sets the start time (not booked yet). Bring a change of clothes and a towel.

items.title: Lunch
items.notes: Before or after kayaking, depending on the tide.

items.title: Drive to Naha and return the car
items.notes: About 2–2½ hours south, partly on the expressway. Fill the tank, return the car, then a taxi or monorail to the hotel.

days.title: Hello, Taipei
days.summary: An early flight to Taiwan. We spend the afternoon in Taipei's old trading district, where 1800s shophouses sell herbs, dried mushrooms and tea, then dive into our first night market. Bring an appetite.

items.title: To Naha Airport
items.notes: An early checkout and a pre-booked taxi to international departures.

items.title: Airport train into Taipei

location.name: Airport Terminal 1 Station
location.address: Dayuan District, Taoyuan City, Taiwan 337

items.notes: After immigration and bags, follow signs for the **Airport MRT** (purple). Buy tokens or tap a card (NT$160 each) and take the **Express** (purple train, fewer stops) from A12 Terminal 1 to **A1 Taipei Main Station**, ~35 minutes. From A1, take a taxi from the rank outside to the hotel — easiest with bags.

items.title: Drop bags at the hotel

location.name: Hotel Royal-Nikko Taipei
location.address: No. 37-1, Section 2, Chung Shan North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei City 104, Taiwan

items.notes: Then lunch nearby.

items.title: Zhongshan cafés and lanes

location.name: Zhongshan Metro Mall
location.address: Zhongshan District, Taipei City, Taiwan 10491

items.notes: Our neighborhood: leafy back lanes full of design shops and good coffee.

items.title: Dihua Street

location.name: Dihua Street
location.address: Section 1, Dihua St, Datong District, Taipei City, Taiwan 103

items.notes: Taipei's oldest street: grand shophouses selling dried fruit, herbs and fabric, with tea houses and boutiques tucked into the courtyards. Taxi, or Green Line to Beimen.

items.title: Ningxia Night Market

location.name: Ningxia Night Market
location.address: Ningxia Rd, Xingming Village, Datong District, Taipei City, Taiwan 103

items.notes: A street full of steaming stalls: oyster omelets, taro balls, grilled squid, bubble tea. Bring cash and share everything.

days.title: Temples, history and Taipei 101
days.summary: Classic Taipei: a vast memorial hall, an ornate temple full of incense, an old brick street, and then up Taipei 101 — once the world's tallest building — for the city lights.

items.title: Metro to Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall

location.name: Zhongshan Station
location.address: No. 16, Nanjing W Rd, Zhongshan District, Taipei City, Taiwan 10491

items.notes: Walk to Zhongshan Station; Red Line toward Xiangshan, 3 stops.

items.title: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall

location.name: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
location.address: Zhongzheng District, Taipei City, Taiwan 100

items.notes: A huge white monument with a blue roof, set in a grand plaza between an opera house and a concert hall. Free.

items.title: Longshan Temple

location.name: Longshan Temple
location.address: No. 211, Guangzhou St, Wanhua District, Taipei City, Taiwan 10853

items.notes: Taipei's most beloved temple, with dragons on every roofline, swirls of incense and locals praying. Green Line to Ximen, then Blue one stop.

items.title: Bopiliao Historic Block

location.name: Bopiliao Historic Block
location.address: Lane 173, Kangding Rd, Fuyin Village, Wanhua District, Taipei City, Taiwan 108

items.notes: A preserved red-brick street from the Qing and Japanese eras. Free.

items.title: Xinyi district
items.notes: Blue Line east to Taipei City Hall. Taipei's glossy modern side: plazas, malls and cafés.

items.title: Up Taipei 101

location.name: Taipei 101 Observatory
location.address: 110, Taiwan, Taipei City, Xinyi District, Xicun Village, Section 5, Xinyi Rd, 7號89樓

items.notes: The world's fastest elevators zip us up 89 floors in under a minute. Watch the city light up, and see the giant golden ball that keeps the tower steady in typhoons. NT$600 each; entrance currently at Office Tower 1F.

days.title: Treasures and hot springs
days.summary: The morning with an emperor's treasure — the National Palace Museum holds the old imperial collection of China. In the afternoon, up into the hills of Beitou, Taipei's hot-spring town, ending with a private soak just for the two of us.

items.title: National Palace Museum

location.name: National Palace Museum
location.address: No. 221, Sec 2, Zhi Shan Rd, Shilin District, Taipei City, Taiwan 111

items.notes: A 30–45 minute taxi. Thousands of years of jade, bronze and porcelain, and, if it's on display, the famous Jadeite Cabbage. NT$350 each.

items.title: Beitou Park, Hot Spring Museum, Thermal Valley

location.name: Beitou Hot Spring Museum
location.address: No. 2, Zhongshan Rd, Linquan Village, Beitou District, Taipei City, Taiwan 112

items.notes: A taxi up to Beitou. A 1913 Japanese bathhouse turned museum, then a steaming jade-green thermal lake. All free.

items.title: Private hot-spring soak

location.name: Grand View Resort Beitou
location.address: No. 30號, Youya Rd, Linquan Village, Beitou District, Taipei City, Taiwan 112

items.notes: Our own private hot-spring room for 90 minutes, up in the hills. A short taxi uphill from Xinbeitou. **Booking opens Oct 11.**

items.title: Dinner
items.notes: In Beitou, or back in Zhongshan.

days.title: One last Taipei morning
days.summary: A lazy last morning at Huashan, an old wine factory turned creative park full of design shops and exhibitions, then back to Okinawa for the night.

location.name: Hotel Royal-Nikko Taipei
location.address: No. 37-1, Section 2, Chung Shan North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei City 104, Taiwan

items.title: Huashan 1914 Creative Park

location.name: Huashan 1914 Creative Park
location.address: No. 1號, Section 1, Bade Rd, Meihua Village, Zhongzheng District, Taipei City, Taiwan 100

items.notes: Brick warehouses full of local designers, pop-up shows and cafés. Taxi, or MRT to Zhongxiao Xinsheng Exit 1.

items.title: Back to the airport

location.name: Hotel Royal-Nikko Taipei
location.address: No. 37-1, Section 2, Chung Shan North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei City 104, Taiwan

items.notes: Collect bags, taxi to A1 Taipei Main, then the Airport MRT Express to A12 Terminal 1.

items.title: Airport to Blossom Naha

location.name: JR Kyushu Hotel Blossom Naha
location.address: 2-16-1 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa

items.notes: A taxi is easiest this late. Or the monorail toward Tedako-Uranishi to **Miebashi**, then a 5-minute walk.

days.title: Homeward
days.summary: A sunrise taxi to the airport and the long way home via Taipei, landing in Chicago the same evening with a camera roll full of memories.

items.title: To Naha Airport
items.notes: Taxi from the hotel, or walk to Miebashi and take the monorail to the airport.
